feedback: Accepted. (1) Format: header REWARD_MACHINE with STATES, INITIAL_STATE, nonempty FINAL_STATES (u3, declared and accepting: agent reached the goal), TRANSITION_FUNCTION in (state, label) -> state form, and REWARD_FUNCTION in (source, label, target) -> reward form; all entries parse. (2) Semantic fidelity: the chain has_key -> door_open -> at_goal matches 'grab the key first, then make your way to the goal'. Including the door milestone is justified, not over-decomposition: at_goal cannot occur before door_open (no other gap in the wall), so every successful policy passes through it, and it matches the example task 'open the door after acquiring the key'. No transition ordering violates the environment constraints (door_open cannot precede has_key; at_goal cannot precede door_open; no two labels can co-fire since pickup/drop/toggle/forward are distinct actions). (3) Persistent/event distinctions: labels are single propositions from the vocabulary, predicate-only; the one-step event key_lost is irrelevant to progression and is correctly absorbed by the (u1, else) self-loop; re-picking up the key in u1 or re-opening the door in u2 hits else with no reward, so there is no double-reward leakage. at_goal is used only in u2 and fires on the terminal step, after which the episode ends, making the absorbing (u3, else) self-loop harmless. (4) Reachability/compactness: u0 -> u1 -> u2 -> u3 is achievable in every variant (key accessible on the starting side, nothing relocks the door, so a re-closed door in u2 can be reopened and the RM correctly stays in u2 with no reward); four states are the minimum for this ordered three-milestone decomposition, no unreachable or redundant states. (5) Reward safety: 0.1, 0.2, 1.0 are monotone toward the goal, strictly positive only on progress transitions, total bounded at 1.3, no negative or self-loop rewards; no regression transitions are required because dropping the key before opening (key_lost) and re-closing the door never block eventual completion and carry no reward here.

All four environment-declared propositions (has_key, door_open, at_goal, key_lost) are implemented and no extra functions are present. Alignment and boolean fidelity check out: has_key matches the documented carrying check (carrying is not None, type 'key', color 'yellow'); door_open scans the full grid with None-guards for an open door (valid with a single door); at_goal inspects the grid cell at env.agent_pos via grid.get(*agent_pos), which is correct because the goal object stays on the grid under the agent; key_lost matches the event reading exactly (prev['has_key'] true, current has_key false, current door_open false), comparing against the read-only previous_valuation snapshot without lingering. key_lost uses only documented API surface (episode_memory['previous_valuation'] read, carrying, grid.get, width, height), guards the snapshot access defensively, and wraps the result in bool() so the return is always a boolean. All syntax is valid, executes without imports, and no function mutates the environment, the grid, or episode memory.
